headline: Tidal Chart Verification Mandatory for Ocean Floor Access
reservation: No advance booking is currently required for general park entry, but admission tickets are valid for two consecutive days to allow for viewing both high and low tides. Access to the ocean floor is strictly governed by the tidal cycle; check the official tide tables before your visit as the beach is cleared as the water rises. Different rules may apply for guided kayak tours which require separate private bookings.

days.title: The Bay of Fundy Cycle

stops.name: Flowerpot Rocks
stops.detail: Walk among the massive sea stacks at low tide to witness the scale of erosion caused by the world's highest tides.

stops.name: Demoiselle Beach
stops.detail: Explore the southern end of the park for a different perspective of the cliffs and salt marshes.

days.driving: Allow 50 minutes from Moncton; traffic is generally light on Route 114.
days.note: Walking on the ocean floor is muddy; wear appropriate footwear and check the 'tide clock' at the visitor center.

days.title: Coastal Cliffs and Kayaking

stops.name: High Tide Kayak Excursion
stops.detail: Paddle around the summits of the same sea stacks you walked beneath the previous day, provided weather allows.

stops.name: Diamond Rock Lookout
stops.detail: Observe the powerful tidal bore from an elevated platform as the Bay of Fundy refills the basin.

days.driving: Minimal local driving; most travel is via park trails or shuttle.
days.note: Kayak tours are highly dependent on wind and weather conditions; verify with local outfitters.

days.title: Hillsborough Highlands

stops.name: Albert County Museum
stops.detail: Understand the local maritime history and the geological formation of the Hopewell Cape region.

stops.name: Gray's Island Lookout
stops.detail: View the expansive marshlands that characterize the upper Bay of Fundy ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between Hillsborough and the park; conditions vary.
days.note: The museum and certain lookouts have seasonal operating hours; check availability locally.

intel.title: Main Gate Capacity
intel.text: Parking is ample at the main visitor center, though the lower lot near the stairs fills first. A motorized shuttle is available for those who wish to bypass the walk from the parking area to the cliff stairs.

intel.title: Cliffside Coverage
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable at the visitor center and upper lookouts. Signal may drop or become intermittent when walking directly beneath the high conglomerate cliffs at low tide.

intel.title: Hillsborough Services
intel.text: Fuel and basic amenities are available in the town of Hillsborough, approximately 10 minutes away. Ensure you have sufficient fuel if continuing south toward Alma or Fundy National Park.

intel.title: Tidal Windows
intel.text: The 'walk on the ocean floor' window typically opens 3 hours before low tide and closes 3 hours after. Safety officers will signal when it is time to exit the beach as the tide returns rapidly.

intel.title: Stairway and Surface
intel.text: Access to the sea floor is via a series of metal staircases which can be slippery when wet. The ocean floor consists of slick mud and loose rocks; stable footwear is essential for safety.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Moncton Airport and pick up supplies in Riverview before heading south on Route 114 to Hopewell Cape.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal; RV parking is designated in the rear of the main lot.
plan.goldenHour: The North Beach area offers dramatic shadows across the sea stacks during the late afternoon low tide in summer.
